name: Loops & Conditionals
description: Five short problems whose only job is to get you writing correct loops and boundary conditions without thinking about efficiency.

name: Basic Maths
description: Digit extraction, divisibility and overflow discipline. Small problems that quietly teach you to reason about numbers rather than iterate over them.

name: Basic Recursion
description: Three problems that establish the shape of a recursive function: a base case, one smaller call, and a combination step.

name: Basic Hashing
description: Your first encounters with the hash map and hash set. Nearly every optimisation later in the roadmap starts with "store what you have already seen".

name: Sorting Algorithms From Scratch
description: Implement each sort yourself. You will rarely ship these, but the invariants they teach show up everywhere.

name: Sorting Applied
description: Problems where the whole difficulty disappears once you sort by the right key, or where you must sort under a custom rule.

name: Easy Arrays
description: Single-pass scans, in-place rewrites and index-as-hash tricks. Master these and the medium tier stops feeling like a jump.

name: Medium Arrays
description: Where arrays get interesting: prefix products, in-place matrix transforms, interval merging and the hash-map-of-prefix-sums idea you will reuse constantly.

name: Hard Arrays
description: Counting problems that need a modified merge sort, geometric reasoning, and the two-sided scans behind trapping rain water.

name: Binary Search on 1D Arrays
description: Get the boundary conventions right here, once, and the rest of the topic becomes mechanical.

name: Binary Search on the Answer
description: The pattern that unlocks a whole class of problems: define a monotone feasibility check, then binary search the answer space instead of the data.

name: Binary Search on Matrices
description: Two shapes of sorted matrix, two very different techniques — plus searching a value range when the data itself is not directly searchable.

name: Easy Strings
description: Scanning, counting and comparing. The skill being built here is enumerating edge cases before you write a line.

name: Medium & Hard Strings
description: Expansion around centres, grouping by canonical form, and the parsing problems that reward writing the specification down first.

name: Singly Linked List Basics
description: Traversal, deletion, reversal and cycle detection. The foundation everything else in this topic builds on.

name: Doubly & Circular Lists
description: Two pointers per node changes what is cheap. These problems show why the operating-system and browser worlds are full of doubly linked lists.

name: Medium Linked Lists
description: Arithmetic on lists, partitioning, sorting in place, and the deep-copy problem that teaches you the interleaving trick.

name: Hard Linked Lists & Caches
description: Group reversal and the two cache designs that come up in system-design interviews as often as in algorithm rounds.

name: Recursion Patterns
description: Halving, doubling and self-similar structure. Each of these has an obvious slow recursion and a much smaller one hiding behind it.

name: Recursion on Strings & Nested Data
description: When the input itself is recursive — nested brackets, nested lists, chemical formulae — the parser wants to be recursive too.

name: Divide & Conquer
description: Split, solve, combine — where the interesting work always lives in the combine step.

name: Subsets & Combinations
description: The take-it-or-leave-it recursion tree, plus the duplicate-skipping rule that stops it emitting the same answer twice.

name: Permutations & Partitions
description: Ordering matters here, and so does the cut point. Both need the same swap-recurse-unswap discipline.

name: Constraint Search
description: The classic hard backtracking set, where the difference between passing and timing out is entirely about pruning.

name: Bit Basics
description: The operations themselves. Short problems chosen so the trick is visible the moment you write the numbers in binary.

name: Bit Tricks & XOR
description: Where bit manipulation stops being a party trick: counting modulo three per bit position, and doing arithmetic without arithmetic operators.

name: Implementations & Design
description: Build the structures before you use them. The amortised argument behind two-stack queues is worth understanding properly.

name: Brackets & Expression Evaluation
description: The canonical use of a stack: matching what is open against what closes it, and evaluating expressions without building a parse tree.

name: Monotonic Stack
description: One idea, nine problems. Keep the stack sorted, and the moment you pop something you have found its nearest greater or smaller neighbour.

name: Stack & Queue Applications
description: Problems that do not look like stack problems until you notice something is waiting to be resolved.

name: Two Pointers
description: Sort first, then let the comparison tell you which pointer to move. The k-sum family is the best drill for this.

name: Sliding Window
description: Expand right greedily, shrink left only while invalid, and keep a summary so every move is constant time.

name: Heap Basics
description: Get comfortable with push, pop and the bounded-size heap before the harder combinations.

name: Top-K & Frequency
description: Counting plus a heap, or counting plus buckets. Knowing when bucketing beats the heap is the real lesson here.

name: Advanced Heap Problems
description: Two heaps facing each other, heaps combined with sorting, and heaps driving a greedy schedule.

name: Classic Greedy
description: Reachability, intervals and partitions — the problems where the greedy rule is provable in a sentence.

name: Scheduling & Exchange Arguments
description: Resource allocation problems where sorting by the right key is the entire algorithm.

name: Traversals
description: Depth-first in three orders, breadth-first level by level, and the views that fall out of them.

name: Tree Properties
description: Height, balance, symmetry and equality. All of them are one postorder pass with a carefully chosen return value.

name: Paths & Ancestors
description: Where the answer bends at a node rather than running straight down. The return value and the shared best become two different things.

name: Construction & Serialization
description: Rebuilding a tree from traversals, flattening it, and turning it into a string and back again.

name: BST Fundamentals
description: Search, insert, delete and validate. Validation is the one people get wrong, because it is not a local check.

name: BST Applications
description: Order statistics, iterators and repair. All of them lean on inorder producing a sorted sequence.

name: Representation & Traversal
description: Adjacency lists, implicit grid graphs, and the two traversals everything else is built on.

name: BFS on Grids & Unweighted Graphs
description: When every move costs the same, breadth-first search is the shortest path. Multi-source BFS is the variant worth learning properly.

name: Cycle Detection & Topological Sort
description: Dependency problems in disguise. If the ordering cannot be completed, you have found a cycle.

name: Shortest Path Algorithms
description: Weighted graphs: the priority-queue algorithm, the negative-weight one, the all-pairs one, and the variants that bend the distance metric.

name: Disjoint Set & Minimum Spanning Tree
description: Merging groups and answering connectivity online — plus the two spanning-tree algorithms that both rest on the cut property.

name: Advanced Graph Algorithms
description: Low-link values, component condensation and Eulerian paths — the algorithms that separate a strong graph round from an average one.

name: 1D Dynamic Programming
description: One index, one decision. Start here and do not move on until the recursion-to-table conversion feels mechanical.

name: DP on Grids
description: Two indices instead of one. The fill order matters more than the recurrence.

name: Subsequences & Knapsack
description: The take-or-skip recurrence, and the capacity dimension that makes it a knapsack. This family covers an enormous share of interview DP.

name: DP on Strings
description: Aligning two sequences prefix by prefix. Once the base row and column are right, the interior is one recurrence.

name: DP on Stocks
description: A small state machine per day. Learn the two-state version and the rest are extra dimensions.

name: Longest Increasing Subsequence Family
description: Start with the quadratic version so you understand it, then learn the patience-sorting speed-up.

name: Partition DP
description: The state is a range and the choice is where to cut it. Cubic time, and the hardest DP family to spot.

name: DP on Squares & Bitmask DP
description: Anchoring shapes at a corner, and encoding "which items are used" as an integer.

name: Trie Fundamentals
description: Build one from scratch, then extend it with wildcards and dictionary lookups.

name: Trie Applications
description: Binary tries over bit representations, and the prefix tree behind a search box.

name: Range Query Structures
description: Segment trees, Fenwick trees and the interval bookkeeping that hides behind calendar problems.

name: Advanced Techniques
description: Binary search on a value range, rolling hashes and two designs that reward careful invariants.
